key_insight: SCAPS-1D simulations show that an In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 stack can strongly improve carrier selectivity and drive CNGS thin-film cells to high predicted efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The study provides design rules for absorber thickness, doping, defect control, and contact engineering that can guide fabrication of higher-performance, earth-abundant thin-film photovoltaics.
method: Modeled a Cu2NiGeS4 absorber with In2S3 electron-transport and MoTe2 hole-transport layers in SCAPS-1D.
Analyzed band alignment, electric-field profiles, carrier distributions, and generation-recombination behavior.
Swept thickness, doping, defect density, recombination, resistance, temperature, and illumination to identify performance-limiting factors.
evidence_signal: Under AM1.5G illumination at 300 K, the optimized device is predicted to reach 28.44% PCE with VOC 0.984 V, JSC 34.39 mA/cm2, and FF 84.04%, exceeding the 6.25–21.17% range reported for prior CNGS designs in the paper.
watch_item: Because the results are purely computational, experimental validation is still needed to confirm interface quality, defect control, and the practical stability of the proposed layer stack.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
